o.text: From Persian جیب, from Arabic جَيْب (jayb).

From Proto-Turkic *yag- (“to rain”).
Cognate with Turkish yağmak, Kazakh жауу (jawuw), Chuvash ҫу (śu), etc.

From Proto-Turkic *kīŕ (“a kind of box; to hide; mystery”) + -lə, whence also Azerbaijani gizli (“hidden”). The original meaning must have meant “to put in a box or bag, to store”.
Cognate with Karakhanid کِزْ (kiz, “a sort of box”), Turkish gizlemek and Turkmen gīzlemek (“to hide”), Turkish giz (“secret”), Dolgan and Yakut кистээ (kistee, “to hide”). Also cognate with Crimean Tatar gizlemek, which is possibly from Ottoman Turkish كیزلمك (“gizlemek”).
Borrowed from Russian провока́ция (provokácija), ultimately from Late Latin provocatio.

Borrowed from Classical Persian چَارْمِیخ (čārmīx, literally “four nails”).
Borrowed from Russian аэролитология (aerolitologija). By surface analysis, aerolit + -logiya.
Borrowed from Russian агробиология (agrobiologija). By surface analysis, aqro- + biologiya (“biology”).
